target_state: implemented staging handoff. The complete body is 112 instructions / 325 bytes, 0x00a980b0..0x00a981f4 inclusive, re-read from the image bytes for this package with objdump and agreeing instruction for instruction with the committed listing. The body is a one-shot initialiser: it tests a byte of its receiver, and if that byte is already non-zero it returns having done nothing at all; otherwise it latches the byte, stores +0.0f at the receiver's +0x14, asks a global singleton accessor for a service object, and if the service is non-null broadcasts between zero and four calls through ONE dispatch slot of that service. The reconstruction is void-returning; the machine ABI record's naming of XMM0 as the return register is the inference's RT1 heuristic firing on the presence of an SSE instruction, and that disagreement is recorded in unresolved_questions rather than resolved by inventing a type.

intended_paths.status: staging-only handoff; src/ is integrator-owned and was not touched, no other package's files were touched, nothing was committed, and Ghidra was not restarted.

implementation.declaration: extern "C" void PKG_SW2_00A980B0_THISCALL re_00a980b0(Receiver* receiver, Word stack_argument)
implementation.argument_surface: Two words at the source level and both are machine-observed rather than guessed. The receiver arrives in ECX (0x00a980b4 `MOV EDI,ECX` is the second instruction, and ECX is never reloaded from anywhere afterwards) and is aliased into EDI. The second word is the single ordinary stack argument named by the terminator's immediate, 0x00a981f2 `C2 04 00` = `RET 0x4`; no instruction in the 112 reads it, so it is declared and left unnamed and the model test drives two different values of it to show the body ignores it. The three indirect calls each push three more words and their callee pops them, which is what keeps the frame balanced through 0x00a981ef `ADD ESP,0x50` and 0x00a981f2 `RET 0x4`; that fixes their convention as __thiscall too rather than cdecl.
implementation.return_note: The body produces nothing for a caller. 0x00a980c0 `XORPS XMM0,XMM0` is the only definition of XMM0 in the body and its result is consumed one instruction later by the store at 0x00a980c9, never read again; the 0x00a980ba `JNZ` path to 0x00a981ee never writes XMM0 at all, so a caller taking the early exit receives whatever XMM0 it arrived with; and the results of all four indirect calls are discarded (the instruction after each `CALL EDX` either reloads EAX from the receiver at 0x00a9816c or falls into the epilogue). The machine record disagrees: abi.return_register is XMM0, abi.return_semantics is float_or_x87_in_XMM0, abi.return.register_class is float_or_x87 and abi.return.void_possible is false, all at APPROXIMATION confidence and all produced by inference RT1, whose own stated basis is 'an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body'. Those are machine-vocabulary phrases no C++ type can equal, so no spelling of the source could have satisfied the record; the type declared here is the one the bytes support and the disagreement is stated rather than papered over. See unresolved_questions.
implementation.receiver_model: An opaque 0x54-byte run with NO named member, reached only through displacement-named accessors. The body touches five displacements on it: +0x0c (read, and the word is a POINTER -- two levels), +0x10 (byte read at 0x00a980b6, byte write of 1 at 0x00a980c5), +0x14 (four-byte MOVSS write of +0.0f at 0x00a980c9), +0x18 (address taken by LEA at 0x00a98152 and NEVER read) and +0x50 (dword read at 0x00a9814b). 0x54 is this body's own bound and no other listing's: the highest displacement it reaches is 0x50 and it reads four bytes there, and the machine record's max_offset is 80 == 0x50, which agrees. abi.receiver carries bounds_only true with offsets [12,16,20,80] and register ECX, so it states where the body was seen reaching and not which member is which, and no member is named.
implementation.dispatch_model: Four sites, all `CALL EDX`, all the same two-level shape: the service's leading word at displacement 0 (0x00a98159, 0x00a98175, 0x00a9819e, 0x00a981cc -- four separate `MOV EDX,[ESI]`, re-read before every call and never hoisted) and then the word at displacement 0x14 of that table (0x00a9815e and its three twins), i.e. slot index 5. Receiver in ECX is the service, unchanged from 0x00a980d3. Three stack arguments per site, pushed right to left, with argument 3 being the zero EBP holds from 0x00a980d5. The machine dispatch record agrees on the count: abi_derived.dispatch reports indirect_calls 4, call_offsets [], vtable_shaped_loads 0. The model re-reads the lead at every site rather than once, and the model test proves the dependence with a hook that swaps the table during the first call and a second invocation whose service points at the other table from the outset.
implementation.dependency_note: One direct callee, declared in the header as ServiceAccessor and DEFINED BY THE MODEL TEST, so the test controls both the service and the null exit at 0x00a980d9. It is named acquire_00883860 after the address 0x00a980ce calls. Read from the image it is two instructions -- `mov eax,ds:0x16514cc; ret` -- a no-argument, caller-cleanup global singleton getter; the neighbouring 0x00883870 is the matching setter and returns the previous value. So the body's null test at 0x00a980d9 is a test for 'no singleton installed yet'. No C++ class name is claimed for the object it returns and no global is declared by this package, because no instruction in the 112 names one.

observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: EDI. 0x00a980b3 `PUSH EDI` / 0x00a980b4 `MOV EDI,ECX` / 0x00a981ee `POP EDI`. Every receiver access in the body is through EDI, which is why the machine receiver record's own ECX-operand scan finds nothing and the record is shape R-ALIAS; the alias is a frame fact with no other observable.
observed_original_abi.stack_argument_1: entry_ESP + 0x4, 4 bytes, NEVER READ. It exists because 0x00a981f2 is `C2 04 00`, which consumes the return address plus one word. The abi record derives the slot from the terminal immediate alone and says so (`source: ret_immediate`, `observed: false`, `read: false`, confidence APPROXIMATION on inference A1-IMM), and the body confirms it: no instruction names entry_ESP+0x4.
observed_original_abi.return_type_note: void is what the bytes support; the machine's own classification disagrees and is recorded here rather than adopted. The two machine facts: abi_derived.abivariants name XMM0 as the return register with return_semantics float_or_x87_in_XMM0 and abi.return.void_possible false, all at APPROXIMATION confidence from inference RT1, whose stated basis is only that 'an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body'. Against that, the body defines XMM0 exactly once (0x00a980c0 XORPS XMM0,XMM0), consumes it immediately at 0x00a980c9 and never reads it again, and the 0x00a980ba JNZ path to 0x00a981ee never writes it at all. Four of the body's five exit paths reach the same epilogue (0x00a981ef ADD ESP,0x50; 0x00a981f2 RET 0x4), which writes no general-purpose register, and all four indirect calls' results are discarded. So there is no value this body produces for a caller on both paths, and ghidra_function.return_type is `undefined` with return_type_resolved false. This worker took section 7 option (a) of the worker contract: declare the type the listing supports and record the disagreement in unresolved_questions. It did NOT declare a typedef named after the machine phrase, and it did NOT call the function float, because on the early-exit path a float return would hand the caller a value the body never computed.
observed_original_abi.frame_resolution: Entry ESP is 0 in the walk. 0x00a980b0 `SUB ESP,0x50` puts ESP at entry-0x50; 0x00a980b3 `PUSH EDI` at entry-0x54; and on the fall-through path 0x00a980c3 `PUSH EBP` at entry-0x58 and 0x00a980c4 `PUSH ESI` at entry-0x5c. So the body runs at entry-0x5c and the reserved frame is entry-0x50..entry-0x01. Every ESP-relative displacement in the body is resolved against entry-0x5c: [ESP+0x54] = entry-0x08, [ESP+0x1c] = entry-0x40, [ESP+0x24] = entry-0x38, [ESP+0x2c] = entry-0x30, [ESP+0x34] = entry-0x28, [ESP+0x3c] = entry-0x20, [ESP+0x4c] = entry-0x10, [ESP+0x44] = entry-0x18. Inside a call block three words are pushed first, so the addresses move: at 0x00a98162 with ESP at entry-0x60, [ESP+0x20] = entry-0x40; at 0x00a9817b with ESP at entry-0x60, [ESP+0x10] = entry-0x50; and at 0x00a98187 with ESP at entry-0x68, [ESP+0x20] = entry-0x48 and [ESP+0x18] = entry-0x50. The two outgoing buffers are therefore 0x10 bytes at entry-0x50..entry-0x41 and 0x40 bytes at entry-0x40..entry-0x01, and 0x10 + 0x40 == 0x50, so the two account for the whole reserved frame. That exact fit is the evidence for the two sizes and is arithmetic over observed displacements, i.e. INFERRED, corroborated rather than assumed.
observed_original_abi.evidence_level: ABI, frame, listing and byte level: complete and self-consistent, and the frame arithmetic closes to the byte. mechanics.body_shape: 112 instructions, 325 bytes, ten conditional branches, every target inside the body, zero unconditional branches, zero loops and no exception handling. The graph is a chain of four guarded blocks, each falling into the next, plus two early exits. The 0x00a980ba JNZ and the 0x00a980d9 JZ and the 0x00a981ca JZ all land inside 0x00a980b0..0x00a981f2, and there is no target outside it, so the branch graph closes inside the recovered span.
mechanics.frame_and_locals: SUB ESP,0x50 then PUSH EDI/EBP/ESI puts the steady-state ESP at entry-0x5c. Two outgoing buffers, and nothing else: 0x10 bytes at entry-0x50 (the three narrow calls' second argument) and 0x40 bytes at entry-0x40 (the wide call's second argument), summing to exactly the 0x50 reserved. The second dword of each 8-byte slot of the wide buffer, and dwords 2 and 3 of the narrow buffer, are never written by this body.
mechanics.guard: 0x00a980b6 `CMP byte ptr [EDI + 0x10],0x0` / 0x00a980ba `JNZ 0x00a981ee`. A BYTE compare against zero, so ANY non-zero value takes the exit, including one whose only set bit is a bit the body never looks at. The exit lands on the epilogue's `POP EDI`, so on that path neither PUSH EBP nor PUSH ESI happened and nothing is written at all. The body therefore runs at most once per receiver.
mechanics.latch: 0x00a980c5 `MOV byte ptr [EDI + 0x10],0x1` (C6 47 10 01) is a one-byte store of the literal 1, and it happens after the test and before anything that can fail, so no reachable path leaves the receiver un-latched.
mechanics.float_store: 0x00a980c9 `MOVSS dword ptr [EDI + 0x14],XMM0` (F3 0F 11 47 14) is a four-byte store at the receiver's +0x14 of the scalar XMM0 that 0x00a980c0 `XORPS XMM0,XMM0` just cleared. MOVSS is the 32-bit single-precision form, so the four bytes written are 0x00000000, which is +0.0f read back as a float. It is the last use of XMM0 in the body.
mechanics.service_acquisition: 0x00a980ce `CALL 0x00883860`, the body's only direct transfer (ghidra_function.callees and the xref export both list it and nothing else), then 0x00a980d3 `MOV ESI,EAX`. In the image the callee is `mov eax,ds:0x16514cc; ret` -- a global singleton getter taking no arguments and cleaning up nothing -- so the null test that follows is a test for 'no singleton installed yet'.
mechanics.null_test: 0x00a980d5 `XOR EBP,EBP` / 0x00a980d7 `CMP ESI,EBP` / 0x00a980d9 `JZ 0x00a981ec`. EBP is zeroed once here and never written again, and it is pushed as the third argument at all four call sites, so every call's third argument is the zero this instruction establishes. The null path lands on the epilogue's `POP ESI`, which means that path runs POP ESI and POP EBP and then falls into POP EDI.
mechanics.attribute_pointer: 0x00a980df `MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDI + 0xc]` loads a POINTER, and the body then reads a second object through it at +0x08 (six times for the flag word), +0x0c, +0x10, +0x14, +0x18, +0x1c and +0x20. The pointer is re-loaded at 0x00a9816c, 0x00a98191 and 0x00a981be, so it is read four times in the body and never cached across a call. This is the two-level point of the body and the model test's first refutation caught a reconstruction that had taken the address of the field instead of its value.
mechanics.flag_word: The word at the attribute object's +0x08 is a bit field and nothing else -- the body never compares it, never uses it arithmetically and never writes it. Nine bits are tested, in the order bit 3, then 0, 1, 2, with bits 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 read inside the bit-3 block. The tests are all `SHR reg,N` followed by `TEST reg8,0x1` on a single byte (or, for bit 0, `TEST byte ptr [EAX + 0x8],0x1` with no shift), so each is an unsigned one-bit test and there is no signedness, threshold or comparison anywhere. BIT 4 IS NEVER TESTED: the shift immediates in the body are 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 4 is absent, so no displacement in the reconstruction is gated on bit 4.
mechanics.wide_call: Gated on bit 3 at 0x00a980e2/0x00a980e5/0x00a980e8/0x00a980eb. When the gate is clear the body jumps to 0x00a9816c, so NONE of the five fill tests is even evaluated -- the gate decides whether the CALL happens, not merely whether the fills do. When it is set: 0x00a980ed stores the literal zero at base+0x38 FIRST, before any flag test; bits 5..9 conditionally copy five consecutive dwords of the attribute object (at +0x10, +0x14, +0x18, +0x1c, +0x20) into base+0x00, +0x08, +0x10, +0x18 and +0x20 respectively; 0x00a9814e then stores the receiver's own +0x50 word at base+0x30 unconditionally; and 0x00a98155 stores the ADDRESS of the receiver's +0x18 at base+0x28 unconditionally, from a LEA, so the word at +0x18 is never read. The call is then 0x00a9816a `CALL EDX` with argument 1 = the attribute object's +0x0c word (0x00a9815b), argument 2 = the 0x40-byte buffer (0x00a98162 `LEA ECX,[ESP + 0x20]` with ESP at entry-0x60), argument 3 = EBP's zero, and ECX = the service.
mechanics.narrow_calls: Three blocks, each re-reading the receiver's +0x0c and the attribute object's +0x08, each gated on bit 0, 1 or 2, each passing the SAME 0x10 bytes at entry-0x50 as argument 2. Each writes the buffer's +0x04 word to EBP's zero FIRST and its +0x00 word SECOND, and both stores happen after all three arguments are already on the stack. The three sites are distinguished by (first argument, selector) as (0x0e7a8471, 0), (0x0e7a8471, 1) and (0x0e7a8473, 2) -- the first and third arguments do NOT move in step with each other, which is a fact of 0x00a98180, 0x00a981a9 and 0x00a981d7 and is the reason the model test checks both halves of each pair independently.
mechanics.result_discarded: The instruction after each of the four `CALL EDX` sites either reloads EAX from the receiver (0x00a9816c) or falls into the epilogue (0x00a981ec), and no EAX a callee leaves is read. So the body uses nothing any callee returns, which is the third and independent leg of the void return type.
mechanics.epilogue: 0x00a981ec `POP ESI`, 0x00a981ed `POP EBP`, 0x00a981ee `POP EDI`, 0x00a981ef `ADD ESP,0x50`, 0x00a981f2 `RET 0x4`. The three exits do not all run it: the guard's path enters at 0x00a981ee and skips the first two, the null and last-gate paths enter at 0x00a981ec and run all three. No general-purpose register is written by any of the five instructions, so whatever a caller receives in EAX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI or EBP is what it left there.
mechanics.globals: None in this body. See observed_original_abi.globals for why 0x16514cc is the callee's evidence and not this body's.
mechanics.vtable_membership: This body is itself an entry of vtable 0x01458788, and the association is verified against the image rather than taken from the classifier: the xref export carries exactly one edge for this VA, `data` from 0x01458790, and the dword at 0x01458788+0x08 is 0x00a980b0, so this body is slot index 2 of that table. mechanics.class_identity: Not established, and deliberately not guessed. The table's fifteen entries, the neighbour at +0x04 and the cluster's subsystem label (editor-core) are suggestive and not conclusive, and this binary has no MSVC RTTI to consult.
other_listings_read_for_this_package: 0x00883860 (2 instructions) -- the direct callee. `mov eax,ds:0x16514cc; ret`. A global singleton getter, no arguments, bare RET so caller-cleanup. The reason the body's null test is a 'no singleton installed' test.

0x00883870 (5 instructions) -- the matching setter. `mov ecx,[esp+4]; mov eax,ds:0x16514cc; mov [ds:0x16514cc],ecx; ret`. It returns the PREVIOUS value, which is why the getter's result is a stable handle. Read to corroborate the getter's role and not modelled.

0x00a97700 region (the 0x01458788 constant search hit at 0x00a9775f) -- a FALSE POSITIVE of the immediate search, inside `f3 0f 11 46 18` (`MOVSS dword ptr [ESI+0x18],XMM0`), whose bytes happen to contain 0x01458788. return_semantics.value: No value. The body's only XMM0 definition is the constant materialisation at 0x00a980c0 for the store at 0x00a980c9; the early-exit path never writes XMM0; all four indirect calls' results are discarded; and the epilogue writes no general-purpose register. A caller cannot read a value this body produced on both paths, and on one of the five exits it would read whatever it brought in.
return_semantics.ownership: Not applicable. The body allocates nothing, returns no address, and hands out one interior address (the receiver's +0x18) that it does not own and does not free.
return_semantics.lifetime: The two outgoing buffers are the body's own frame storage and die with the call; the callee is given a pointer to them and may not retain it. Nothing the body stores survives except the receiver's +0x10 byte and its +0x14 dword.

evidence.decompiler: Available and consistent with the listing. Ghidra's C for this body (ghidra_function, categories.decompilation) agrees with the reconstruction on every branch condition, every displacement, both call shapes, the argument order at all four sites and the fact that the two pushed immediates differ between the second and third narrow site. Where the decompiler's naming is a guess rather than a reading it was NOT adopted: its local_50/local_48 and local_40/local_38/... names are Ghidra's own frame-splitting, and its `local_8`/`local_10`/`local_18` grouping does not correspond to the two buffers this package derives from the ESP-relative displacements. The reconstruction's two-buffer reading (0x10 at entry-0x50, 0x40 at entry-0x40) comes from the frame arithmetic, not from the decompiler.
evidence.decompiler_disagreements: One worth recording. The decompiler types receiver+0x14 as an undefined4 rather than a float, and it types the wide buffer's argument as a struct it names local_40 -- but it also drops the gate: its reconstruction of the big-struct block has the bit-3 test as the block's entry condition and the five fills inside, which is the same control flow this package derives. There is no disagreement about behaviour; only about type names, and the package claims no types.
